distinctions_drawn: Real an sich vs. Real phenomenon
explicit_definitions_given: Real an sich: unconditioned transcendent ground, unknowable in itself
Real phenomenon: culturally conditioned manifestation of the Real
sensus divinitatis: universal human capacity to experience the transcendent
soteriological transformation: shift from self-centeredness to Reality-centeredness

objections_raised: Hick's exclusion of pre-axial traditions is arbitrary
Hick's axial privilege is historically and metaphysically unjustified

philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: philosophy of religion, religious pluralism, soteriology, epistemology of religious experience

summary_of_core_decisions: The text argues that Hick's pluralism is internally incoherent because it combines a universal epistemological capacity for experiencing the Real with a soteriological criterion that arbitrarily excludes pre-axial and indigenous traditions. It then proposes two modifications: broadening the soteriological criterion to include ecological and communal flourishing, and expanding the phenomenal categories of the Real to include animistic and shamanic experiences.
